From b9ddd5091160793ee9fac10da765cf3f53d2aaf0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jacopo Mondi <jacopo+renesas@jmondi.org>
Date: Mon, 5 Aug 2019 17:55:15 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] iio: adc: max9611: Fix temperature reading in probe

The max9611 driver reads the die temperature at probe time to validate
the communication channel. Use the actual read value to perform the test
instead of the read function return value, which was mistakenly used so
far.

The temperature reading test was only successful because the 0 return
value is in the range of supported temperatures.

Fixes: 69780a3bbc0b ("iio: adc: Add Maxim max9611 ADC driver")
Signed-off-by: Jacopo Mondi <jacopo+renesas@jmondi.org>
Cc: <Stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iio/adc/max9611.c b/drivers/iio/adc/max9611.c
index 0e3c6529fc4c..da073d72f649 100644
--- a/drivers/iio/adc/max9611.c
+++ b/drivers/iio/adc/max9611.c
@@ -480,7 +480,7 @@ static int max9611_init(struct max9611_dev *max9611)
 	if (ret)
 		return ret;
 
-	regval = ret & MAX9611_TEMP_MASK;
+	regval &= MAX9611_TEMP_MASK;
 
 	if ((regval > MAX9611_TEMP_MAX_POS &&
 	     regval < MAX9611_TEMP_MIN_NEG) ||
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/iio/adc/max9611.c`**
- The line that previously assigned the return value of a function to `regval` has been modified. Instead of using `regval = ret & MAX9611_TEMP_MASK;`, the code now uses `regval &= MAX9611_TEMP_MASK;`. 
- This change ensures that the actual read value (stored in `ret`) is not mistakenly used for the temperature reading test. Instead, it correctly applies the mask to the existing value of `regval`.

### Relationships
The modification in the `max9611.c` file addresses a bug where the temperature reading validation was incorrectly relying on the return value of a function rather than the actual temperature data. By changing the assignment to a bitwise AND operation, the patch ensures that the temperature reading is validated against the correct data, thus fixing the issue that allowed the test to pass erroneously when it should not have. This change is crucial for the proper functioning of the driver, as it directly impacts the accuracy of temperature readings during the probe phase.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
ret = max9611_read_single(max9611, CONF_TEMP, &regval);
regval = ret & MAX9611_TEMP_MASK;
```
Reason:
The first statement reads the temperature value into `regval`, but the second statement incorrectly uses the return value `ret` (which could be 0) to mask `regval`. This means that if `ret` is 0, `regval` will also be set to 0, leading to a false validation of the temperature reading, as 0 is within the acceptable range.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
regval &= MAX9611_TEMP_MASK;
```
Reason:
This statement correctly applies the mask to `regval`, which contains the actual temperature data read from the device, rather than using the return value `ret`. This ensures that the validation of the temperature reading is based on the actual data received, preventing incorrect validation and ensuring that the test fails when it should.
